contribution.method:
Batch of 1013 witnesses in 25 problems (`MANIFEST.json` + `records/<record_id>.json` + `SUMMARY.tsv`), each below the current `records/SUMMARY.csv` entry (main at 8ce7b488, checked 2026-10-31). Every record passes `verify_general.py` (VALID) and `certify_general.py` (CERTIFIED) from that commit locally, run on the files extracted from the archive. The changes against the current records: median -0.01 %, largest -3.49 %; 52 records improve by ≥ 1 %, 316 by ≥ 0.1 %.

**Relation to earlier submissions.** #104 was merged and the public records rebuilt in 8ce7b488 (2026-10-30); every record here is below the value in that archive and below the values in open submissions.

**Against PolyPack.** I also compared with PolyPack's published records (https://github.com/sinkomr/PolyPack, `data/polyhedra/records.json`, fetched 2026-10-31) and kept only records that are below both the archive and PolyPack (322 of these records have a PolyPack value; `SUMMARY.tsv` lists both values, `polypack_s`, `change_vs_best`).

**How the records were made.** `found_by`, `credit` and `method` identify where each record starts; `method` or `refinement` gives the steps.

- *Refinements of catalogue records* (703): a contact-preserving descent (sequential linear programming with the contacts as inequalities) started from the catalogue record named in `refinement` (for some, a randomised multi-start search from perturbed copies of that record comes first; `refinement` says so). `found_by`, `credit` and `method` are the catalogue record's own, copied verbatim; my part is in `refined_by` and `refinement_credit`. For 96 of them the start was the record for a different n and the first n pieces were kept (`derived_from`). Rigidity analysis and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23630728
- *Lattice cuts* (214): all pieces in one orientation at the points of a lattice inside the container, orientation and position of the container optimised, then a descent as above.
